key_insight: Introducing a region-graph formulation with optimal transport routing lets a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) aggregator assign spatially coherent WSI regions to specialised experts, preventing imbalanced routing and improving classification and interpretability.
problem_solved: Standard MIL and MoE aggregators route all instances through shared or unconstrained softmax pathways, causing expert collapse, imbalanced workloads, and loss of spatial/contextual structure in gigapixel whole-slide image classification.
method: Construct a region-graph over WSI patches to encode local spatial relationships and reduce noisy per-instance routing.
Use an optimal-transport-based routing layer to assign region mass to experts under capacity and balance constraints, encouraging specialised, spatially coherent expert assignments.
Train end-to-end within the MIL framework so experts learn specialised features and the routing adapts to both task loss and load regularisation.
impact: Enables scalable, balanced MoE deployment for gigapixel pathology images with improved accuracy, interpretability, and resource efficiency—making specialised expert routing practical for real-world WSI pipelines.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram: WSI → patches → region-graph → optimal transport flow → experts → slide-level prediction

Heatmap overlays on slides showing per-expert activation/specialisation regions
Bar chart comparing expert utilization, classification accuracy, and calibration against baseline MIL/MoE methods
paper_title: Region-Graph Optimal Transport Routing for Mixture-of-Experts Whole-Slide Image Classification
paper_authors: Xin Tian, Jiuliu Lu, Ephraim Tsalik, Bart Wanders, Colleen Knoth
